relevance_note: Single case report of a PSTPIP1 variant carrier: 'Trio whole-genome sequencing revealed a de novo heterozygous PSTPIP1 gene variant (NM_003978.5): exon 11: c.748G>A (p.Glu250Lys)'.
method_note: Read the paper by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script from values I read; no table transcribed by script. Scope: the proband ('patient', case-report rule 5) and his two parents (trio-sequenced, described as unaffected; sex not stated, so 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2'). Table 1 lists syndromes and variants, not individuals; Lindor 1997 and other cited cases give no individual-level facts and get no rows. Onset: the abstract states 'disease onset at 13 years of age', but the case presentation says folliculitis-like changes on the legs 'for 10 years' at age 16 (i.e. earlier); I recorded the authors' stated onset (13 years) and flag the discrepancy. De novo recorded because the paper states trio WGS found the variant de novo (both parents sequenced), though it does not separately say each parent was negative. CRP 26.39 mg/L, ESR 50 mm/h, hemoglobin 107 g/L, WBC 3.75 and neutrophils 1.68 x10^9/L are printed without reference ranges or a statement of abnormality; checklist items for inflammatory markers, anemia and neutropenia left 'not reported' (only the earlier 'low level of white blood cell count' is recorded, as a feature). Gastrointestinal endoscopy and bone marrow 'no significant abnormalities' are whole investigations and were recorded as written; IBD left 'not reported' despite hematochezia. 'No superficial lymph node enlargement was palpable' recorded as a feature only; lymphadenopathy checklist left 'not reported' (narrower absence). Calprotectin and zinc were within the paper's stated normal ranges, so hypercalprotectinemia and hyperzincemia are excluded. Parents: 'They both denied having a history of skin or joint diseases' used to exclude arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, acne and hidradenitis suppurativa (broader absence); this is self-report. Pedigree (Figure 1) not readable; no variant rows for parents. The variant type (missense) is not stated by the authors, so variant_type is 'not reported'. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null (no statement either way). No contradictions found apart from the onset discrepancy.

treatment_summary.value: topical ointment; incision and drainage with anti-infective treatment; methylprednisolone 40 mg daily and cyclosporine 75 mg twice daily (unsatisfactory); methylprednisolone increased to 120 mg/day; adalimumab 40 mg every 2 weeks with prednisone 5 mg/day maintenance (PG and abdominal pain relieved, acne did not improve); IL-1 antagonists advised
span: He was treated with topical ointment, but no improvement was observed.
Incision and drainage, along with anti-infective treatment, were performed, but no improvement was observed
Methylprednisolone 40 mg once daily and cyclosporine 75 mg twice daily were administered with unsatisfactory results.

Subsequently, adalimumab 40 mg subcutaneously every 2 weeks was given, and the steroid dosage was gradually reduced to prednisone 5 mg per day for maintenance. His symptoms of PG and abdominal pain were relieved, but severe acne did not improve.
The patient was advised to use IL-1 antagonists for better control of the symptoms.
